title: Direct cell-to-cell transmission of retrotransposons.
data_url: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE292041 (plus GSE292040, GSE292044, PRIDE PXD061763, and Table S1 at https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.03.14.642691v2.supplementary-material)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed Table S1 (xlsx, 6 sheets, 590 protein sequences total: 105 insect LTR-retrotransposon consensus hits, 88 Drosophila melanogaster loci, 306 Aedes aegypti loci, 43 Sitophilus oryzae loci, 9 nackednaviruses, 39 picornaviruses; columns include sequence, length in amino acids, Phobius and TMHMM 2.0c transmembrane-topology predictions, an MGxxxS/T motif flag, species). Downloaded and parsed the GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) processed files: GSE292041_RNAseq_GeTMM.txt.gz = 16,424 genes x 16 samples; one differential-expression table = 10,551 genes with log2 fold change and adjusted p-value; GSE292044 small-RNA table = 122 transposable elements x 6 samples; GSE292040_TE_consensus.fa.gz = 122 transposon consensus sequences. Read the GEO file manifest (raw bigWig coverage tracks, 30-50 MB each; GSE292041_RAW.tar = 2.55 GB). Confirmed PRIDE project PXD061763 exists; its per-file listing endpoint returned empty.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The screening method (8,417 Gypsy/Metaviridae arthropod consensus sequences from Repbase, downloaded March 2024, filtered by open-reading-frame length 60-210 amino acids, single transmembrane helix, N-terminal-outside topology, MGxxxS/T myristoylation motif, cytoplasmic tail under 150 amino acids) and the imaging/electron-microscopy evidence that sORF2 is required for soma-to-germline capsid transfer. The published Cell version is paywalled with no PubMed Central identifier, so its own data-availability statement and supplement were not retrievable; everything above comes from the open bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2025.03.14.642691) of the same study.

a1_downloadable.note: All three GEO series, the Table S1 spreadsheet and the PRIDE proteomics project are public and downloaded without login. Verified in the files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. The biologically interesting label - whether a retrotransposon can move from somatic cells into the germline - is nowhere a column. Table S1 only lists candidates that passed a sequence filter; transmission was shown by microscopy for a handful of elements (412, Stalker2) and would have to be constructed by hand.

a3_inputs_present.note: Amino-acid sequences are present in full in Table S1, and the 122 transposon consensus DNA sequences are in the GEO FASTA file. No identifier lookups needed. Verified in the files.

a4_units_stated.note: Expression table is labelled GeTMM (gene-length-corrected trimmed mean of M-values); small-RNA table states counts per kilobase of element per million microRNAs; sequence lengths in amino acids. Verified in the file headers.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. 590 sequences in Table S1, all positives, dominated by near-identical copies of a few families (306 of them are Aedes aegypti genomic copies of the same handful of elements). The expression data has 16 samples; the small-RNA data has 122 elements x 6 samples. Nothing reaches the ~400-row classification floor once redundancy is removed.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~2.2 MB of processed tables plus a 0.08 MB spreadsheet
a6_fits_laptop.note: Processed files are tiny; only the 2.55 GB raw bigWig archive is large and is not needed. Verified by downloading.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Paper says 105 high-confidence hits across 29 organisms; the Table S1 insect sheet has exactly 105 data rows. Verified.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL, and it is the decisive failure. Membership in Table S1 was decided by running TMHMM 2.0c and Phobius (both transmembrane-helix prediction programs) on the sequence and applying a regular-expression motif search - the label is another model's output computed directly from the features, so a sequence model would only re-learn TMHMM plus a regex.

backbone.name: ESM-2, a protein language model (would have been the natural choice for ~70-100 amino-acid sORF2-like sequences)
backbone.hardware: CPU only would suffice for 590 short sequences
backbone.licence: ESM-2 is MIT-licensed; not pursued because Part A failed

integration.partner_dataset: Repbase/Dfam transposon libraries (8,417 arthropod Gypsy consensus sequences were screened) and UniProt viral fusogen entries
integration.join_key: Repbase element name, and NCBI nucleotide accession for the viral hits
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which transposable elements across insect genomes carry a cell-cell fusogen and can therefore invade the germline from somatic tissue - a real question, but this paper supplies only positives defined by a rule, so the combination cannot be trained or tested honestly.

controls.positive_control: The 412 and Stalker2 elements, shown by imaging to transmit, would have to come out top-ranked; only two such elements exist.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is possible in principle but meaningless with no negative class.
controls.external_validation: The 9 nackednavirus and 39 picornavirus sORF2-like proteins are an independent, non-transposon set - but they were found with the same filter, so they test the filter, not biology.

honest_claim_h3: A model trained on this data could only claim to reproduce the authors' own TMHMM-plus-motif filter on short open reading frames in insect retrotransposons; it could say nothing about which elements actually transmit between cells, because that was measured for only two elements.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a retrotransposon's protein sequence to predict whether it can push its capsids from somatic cells into the egg.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would have shown a model each short protein encoded by an insect retrotransposon - 590 sequences are in the supplementary table, and about 8,417 transposon consensus sequences were screened - with no measured outcome attached to all but two of them.
plain_idea.predict: A yes/no call on whether the element encodes a cell-cell fusion protein and transmits to the germline. The true answer comes from fluorescence and electron microscopy of fly ovaries, done for only a couple of elements.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Knowing which transposons can jump between cells would matter to transposon-biology and antiviral-immunity labs, but the measurement exists for too few elements here to learn or test anything.

label_elsewhere.sources: No public resource records whether a transposable element transmits from soma to germline; transmembrane topology is available from DeepTMHMM and UniProt, but that is the filter, not the biology. Based on the resources I know plus searching the paper's own accessions.
label_elsewhere.join_key: Repbase element name / NCBI nucleotide accession
label_elsewhere.why: The outcome of interest exists only in this paper's microscopy, for a couple of elements, so there is no external training or validation set.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: a protein-language-model classifier (ESM-2 embeddings plus a logistic head) over short open reading frames in insect LTR retrotransposons, to flag sORF2/FAST-like cell-cell fusogens genome-wide. It dies because the only available labels are the output of the authors' own TMHMM 2.0c plus Phobius plus MGxxxS/T-motif rule applied to the same sequences, with no negatives and no measured transmission outcome. A secondary idea - predicting per-element small-RNA silencing from transposon sequence - dies on size: 122 elements and 6 samples.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the files I actually downloaded: 2.2 MB of processed tables and 590 short sequences; ESM-2 small-checkpoint embeddings for 590 sequences of under 150 amino acids take minutes on a laptop CPU. The data is trivially cheap - the problem is that there is nothing honest to learn.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows in Table S1 and read its column headers: 590 positive-only sequences whose two label-defining columns are TMHMM and Phobius predictions. That check takes five minutes and kills the project.

verdict_reason: A mechanistic cell-biology paper, not a modelling dataset. Three Part A killers fail, verified in the files: A8 (the only large label set, Table S1's 590 sequences, was defined by running TMHMM 2.0c and Phobius transmembrane predictors plus a myristoylation-motif regex on the very sequences a model would use as input - a classifier would distil those tools, not learn biology), A2 (the real outcome, soma-to-germline transmission, is not a column and was measured by microscopy for only two elements), and A5 (590 redundant positives with zero negatives; the expression data is 16 samples and the small-RNA data 122 elements). The data itself is exemplary - public GEO series GSE292040/41/44, PRIDE PXD061763, clean units, counts matching the paper - it is simply the wrong shape for supervised learning.
